title: secrets pack: Bash-channel credential scanning
description: Reuses org-rule-guard.py's existing secret-value regex machinery, closes the Bash-channel gap (currently only wired to Write/Edit). Hook-front-end-only -- scans the entire raw Bash command string regardless of executable, which the PATH-wrapper's argv[0]-shadow dispatch structurally cannot do. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Architecture and Phase 1.

title: Genesis: irreversible-command-gate Implementation
description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md (562 lines, 5 gap-review rounds complete as of 2026-08-13)

## Overview
A guard for AI coding/automation agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI) that intercepts commands before execution and blocks/redirects irreversible operations, extending org-rule-guard.py's coverage. Full decomposition: 44 beads total (28 created directly from Phase 0-3's plan content, plus 16 pre-existing beads from two /plan-idea-gen ideation runs, retroactively wired with blocker edges to the infrastructure they actually depend on).

## Progress
- [ ] Phase 0 -- deploy path (icg-ci pipeline, release-integrity Layers 1/2/4, self-updater, release-cutting runbook): 6 beads (icg-4me, icg-52j, icg-1dk, icg-4nu, icg-2nw, icg-24g)
- [ ] Phase 1 -- Tier 1 rules, both front-ends where applicable: 8 infrastructure beads (icg-4vq, icg-2jd, icg-1k0, icg-3my, icg-3q6, icg-6bg, icg-rik, icg-51o) + 8 new content-pack beads (icg-6tj, icg-1bav, icg-4bra, icg-25sg, icg-4nt2, icg-14ff, icg-u34c, icg-shs8) + 2 pre-existing content beads (icg-2m8 git stale-HEAD, icg-1vj misc deprecated-bead-CLI)
- [ ] Phase 2 -- cross-invocation state: 3 beads (icg-1seg state-store, icg-2eu0 flush-before-pull, icg-20ja flush-before-repair)
- [ ] Phase 3 -- redirect-mechanism richness: 3 beads (icg-25u2 updatedInput force-push, icg-50ya additionalContext+Codex-fallback, icg-4338 value-derivation helpers)
- [ ] Phase 4 -- ideation run 1 finalists: 9 pre-existing beads (icg-rri, icg-ncf, icg-2ck, icg-l75, icg-1tj, icg-z5n, icg-2i8, icg-59u, icg-d3i)
- [ ] Phase 5 -- ideation run 2 finalists: 6 pre-existing beads (icg-4p8, icg-2m8 [counted in Phase 1], icg-4bu, icg-3xz, icg-4mu, icg-53q) + 1 done directly (README non-goals section, no bead)

## Flagged gap from decomposition review (fallback role, per user direction)
One real gap found reviewing plan.md against the 44-bead decomposition: icg-4bu's fail-closed transition has an explicit open implementation question in Architecture (docs/plan/plan.md lines ~73-87) -- whether Claude Code's/Codex's own hook-timeout/hook-error config can substitute for a dedicated watchdog process, avoiding the 'standing daemon' architecture ideation explicitly killed elsewhere (Lens-1 idea #69). This verification step (checking both harnesses' actual hook specs) isn't its own trackable bead anywhere -- it's prose inside icg-4bu's blocking Architecture discussion. Whoever picks up icg-4bu should do this verification FIRST, before assuming a watchdog is needed; if neither harness supports it, icg-4bu needs to either accept the standing-daemon cost or get re-scoped. Not spinning up a separate bead for this since it's a research step gating one specific bead's approach, not independent work -- flagged here instead per genesis-bead-as-fallback role.

Everything else reviewed against plan.md's Architecture/Components/Data Models/Phases sections maps cleanly onto an existing bead -- no other coverage gaps found.

title: storage-class pack: ssd/ssd-large detection
description: Content-mode, applies_to *.yaml/*.yml, hook front-end only. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 1.

title: Layer 1: coverage-diff CI gate
description: Structured diff of rule-pack changes between releases -- removed guarded_patterns, widened safe_patterns, narrowed destructive_patterns -- flagged for explicit justification, build-failing icg-ci gate. See docs/notes/release-integrity-verification.md Layer 1. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 0.

title: icg binary: three-dispatch-mode skeleton
description: One binary: (1) invoked under its own name, subcommand dispatch for admin commands (update/status/new-pack/...); (2) invoked under a shadowed tool's name via argv[0] (symlinks earlier in PATH than the real binaries, cargo-precedent shape), runs command-mode checks then execs the real binary; (3) invoked as 'icg hook' by Claude Code/Codex hook wiring, reads PreToolUse JSON from stdin. This bead is just the routing skeleton -- individual subcommands/packs are separate beads. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Components 'icg binary'.

title: State-store component
description: Minimal persistent marker for Tier 2 cross-invocation ordering rules. org-rule-guard.py has no equivalent -- new surface. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Components 'State store', Phase 2.

title: icg status command with blind-spot self-report
description: One command printing current rule-pack version, last successful self-update check, and a hardcoded KNOWN_LIMITATIONS list (cloud-hosted Codex, absolute-path wrapper bypass, etc.). Operationalizes the plan's own 'don't oversell' principle live rather than leaving it as prose a human has to reread. Objection: only as honest as it's kept current -- risks becoming stale documentation with extra steps if not maintained. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #5 (merged #97+#72).

title: Bead-CLI deprecation pack: data-driven, ready for bf-to-bead-rs cutover
description: bead-forge (bf) is being prepared for deprecation in favor of bead-rs (~/bead-rs, binary 'bead', a separate clean-room reimplementation -- NOT the same lineage as the already-deprecated br/beads_rust despite the similar name). Ensure the misc pack's deprecated-bead-CLI rule stores 'currently canonical' and 'deprecated' tool names as pack DATA (a small list), not hardcoded logic naming bf specifically -- so the eventual bf-to-bead cutover is a one-line data update, not a rule rewrite, when bf actually gets deprecated. Do NOT flip the rule to prefer bead over bf yet -- bf remains canonical today per CLAUDE.md, and per reference_needle_bead_rs_compat_gap_2026-08-12.md, bead-rs command syntax genuinely differs from bf's in several places (sync flush-only is a subcommand not a flag, dep add argument order is reversed, no batch/mitosis equivalent) so this is not a drop-in synonym swap. Also verify (currently unconfirmed) that bead-rs uses the same .beads/ directory + git-worktree file-vs-directory convention the beads pack's check (icg's own .git predicate) already assumes -- if it diverges, the beads pack's check needs bead-rs-specific verification too, separate from this misc-pack rule. From user direction 2026-08-13.

title: Rule: deny repair before flush
description: Deny bf doctor --repair unless a flush already happened this session -- flush must come first (opposite polarity from the flush-before-pull rule). Tier 2. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 2.

title: Release-cutting runbook
description: Documented, human-run process: gh release create only once icg-ci (incl. Layer 1 gates) has passed on the target commit and Layer 2 review is done. No additional approval-workflow layer beyond that -- Layers 1/2/4 already sufficient. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 0 'Release-cutting trigger, resolved'.

title: git pack: force-push detection
description: CommandRegex, both front-ends, deny-only for v1 (updatedInput flag-stripping is Phase 3). Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 1.

title: updatedInput: force-push flag-stripping
description: The flagship intent-preserving redirect example: strip --force/-f/--force-with-lease from a git push rather than denying outright. Fires on both front-ends -- needs both redirect-realization beads. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 3.

title: Poison-pill auto-rollback
description: If a fresh release's deny-rate spikes abnormally above a rolling baseline within the first M commands, auto-revert the self-update trust pointer to the prior release and log loudly. Closes a serious gap: a bad release silently degrading the whole fleet at once. Objection: the rollback trigger itself needs to be conservative -- could misfire on a legitimately bad day of command hygiene, not just a bad release. Depends on Phase 0's trust-pointer mechanism existing first. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #3.

title: Rule: deny flush before pull
description: Deny bf sync --flush-only (or bead-rs sync flush-only once cutover happens, see icg-1vj) unless a git pull already happened this session -- pull must come first. Tier 2, opposite polarity from the flush-before-repair rule despite similar naming. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 2.

title: Per-repo signed override
description: An overrides/<repo>.toml schema (which rule IDs are exempted, mandatory expiry date) routed through the same Layer 1/2 release-integrity CI gates as a rule-pack release -- a real escape hatch that doesn't undermine tamper-resistance, not a silent local bypass. Objection: overrides accumulate over time into Swiss-cheese coverage if not actively curated -- needs a forced re-justification cadence, mirroring Layer 1's staleness-flagging philosophy. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #7.

title: Engine: content-mode input handling
description: Reads file path + content from Write/Edit PreToolUse JSON (mirrors org-rule-guard.py's own trigger), matches against content-mode packs (storage-class, image-tag) via applies_to file globs, and against beads pack's predicate. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Components 'Engine'.

title: Stale-HEAD push guard
description: Before allowing git push, compare the local checkout's tracked remote HEAD against the actual current remote HEAD (live check); if they differ, fail the push and redirect the agent to pull and resolve first. Simpler revision of the original shared-tree-collision idea (cross-process /proc scanning), per user direction 2026-08-13. Catches a different failure mode than the documented git-index-race incident (that one was uncommitted work getting swept into another worker's commit within the SAME shared tree, before any push) -- this catches pushing on top of state that's since moved. Deliberate, scoped exception to the no-I/O-in-hot-path engine constraint: git push is already a network operation, so a live remote-HEAD check here doesn't set a precedent for adding I/O to other guarded commands. From /plan-idea-gen run 2 (2026-08-13), docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #2 (revised mechanism).

title: Base self-updater and trust pointer (icg update)
description: User-triggered (not polling) icg update command: checks GitHub Releases API once, downloads the new rule-pack artifact, atomically replaces the on-disk artifact (write-then-rename) -- no persistent process to restart, per-invocation architecture. Trust pointer (Layer 4 minimal form) tracks a separately-advancing release, not bare latest. See docs/notes/self-update-and-release-gating.md and docs/plan/plan.md Components/Phase 0. icg-2ck and icg-l75 extend this once it exists.

title: PATH-wrapper install mechanism
description: Installs symlinks for currently-loaded command-mode packs' tool_keywords (vault/bao/git/etc, docker once icg-d3i ships) earlier in $PATH than the real binaries -- never kubectl. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Architecture 'Integration point'.

title: Claude Code hook adapter install
description: Wires 'icg hook' into Claude Code's settings.json PreToolUse hook config, alongside (not replacing) org-rule-guard.py. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Architecture 'Integration point'.

title: ReDoS check on submitted rule packs
description: CI check in icg-ci flagging catastrophic-backtracking-prone regex patterns in a submitted pack before it ships, via a timeout-bounded fuzz check or a known ReDoS-pattern detector. Defends against an honest authoring mistake, not an adversarial attack -- squarely inside the stated threat model despite superficially sounding like security hardening. From /plan-idea-gen run 2 (2026-08-13), docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #7.

title: Value-derivation helpers
description: Embed the real derivable value in a deny reason instead of pointing at where to look -- e.g. the actual semver from containers/<name>/VERSION for the image-tag rule. Known, consciously-accepted gap in Phase 1 (see Open Questions) that this closes. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Components 'Value-derivation helpers', Phase 3.

title: image-tag pack: both halves (:latest + bare-SHA)
description: Fully absorbs org-rule-guard.py's rule 3, not just the bare-SHA gap -- both :latest re-detection and bare-SHA pinning. Content-mode, hook front-end only. See docs/notes/existing-enforcement-infrastructure.md. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 1.

title: Graduated fail-open to fail-closed policy for guard crashes
description: In the beginning, the guard dying (e.g. OOM-killed mid-check) does NOT halt the fleet -- fails open, matching org-rule-guard.py's existing philosophy. As the guard's reliability is validated over time, shift to a fail-closed posture where the fleet can't run without the guard being healthy. Graduation signal ties to the poison-pill auto-rollback mechanism (icg-2ck) already tracking per-release deny-rate health -- e.g. N consecutive releases with zero poison-pill triggers -- rather than inventing a new maturity signal from scratch; exact threshold TBD at implementation time. From /plan-idea-gen run 2 (2026-08-13), docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #6 (policy per user direction 2026-08-13).

title: icg-ci Argo WorkflowTemplate
description: Rust binary -> GitHub Release pipeline on the existing forge-ci/needle-ci/agentscribe-ci/sigil-ci pattern, in declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/. Never GitHub Actions. Foundational -- every other Phase 0/1 bead depends transitively on this existing. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 0.

title: Per-rule enable/disable feature flag
description: Revised from the original fleet-wide single-rule kill-switch design per user direction 2026-08-13: implement as a feature flag on each guarded_pattern (enabled: true/false), part of normal rule-pack data, toggled through the SAME release-integrity pipeline (Layer 1/2) as any other rule-pack change -- simpler, reuses existing infrastructure, no separate trust-pointer axis. Tradeoff to keep visible: this means disabling a misbehaving rule takes exactly as long as a normal release, which does NOT satisfy the original motivation (stop an actively-harmful rule before the next full release cycle completes). If genuine emergency-speed single-rule disable is ever needed, that's a distinct, unresolved requirement -- not solved by this bead. From /plan-idea-gen run 2 (2026-08-13), docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #8 (revised).

title: beads pack: conjunction check
description: Deny .beads/ writes when (a) target is under .beads/ AND (b) .git at the repo root is a directory (shared/primary tree), not a file (linked worktree). Both conditions required -- (b) alone would over-match almost any normal repo. See docs/notes/beads-protection-scope.md. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Components 'beads pack's check'.

title: Layer 2: review process informed by coverage-diff
description: Human review of a release candidate reads the generated coverage-diff report (bead @2), not raw regex. See docs/notes/release-integrity-verification.md Layer 2. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 0.

title: Guard CI/build pods on iad-ci
description: Extend coverage to Argo Workflow pods, including this project's own icg-ci release pipeline, not just interactive Claude Code/Codex sessions. First step: wire the PATH-wrapper into the shared Argo Workflow executor image. Strongest justification is self-referential -- the release pipeline that guards everything else should itself be guarded. From /plan-idea-gen run 2 (2026-08-13), docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #1.

title: Engine: command-mode input handling
description: Reads a command description from PreToolUse JSON on stdin or wrapped-command argv, segments shell lines like org-rule-guard.py's check_bash (splits on ;/&&/||, skips sudo/env-assignment/wrapper prefixes), basename-matches tokens against tool_keywords, matches against loaded command-mode packs (vault/git/secrets/misc/tmux). Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Components 'Engine'.

title: additionalContext with Codex fallback
description: Non-blocking-warning channel. Codex accepts additionalContext in its hook schema but doesn't yet honor it -- any rule reaching for this channel needs an explicit Codex fallback (most likely downgrading to deny there) rather than assuming parity across harnesses. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 3.

title: Redirect dispatch: PATH-wrapper front-end realization
description: Wrapper-side equivalents with no native JSON protocol: deny = refuse to exec + stderr + non-zero exit; updatedInput = rewrite argv before exec; additionalContext = stderr + exec normally. Needed for Phase 3's flagship force-push-stripping example, which fires on both front-ends. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Components 'Redirect dispatch'.

title: Layer 1: regression-suite CI gate
description: A fixed deny-must-still-fire regression suite, run by icg-ci, build-failing if any previously-covered case is no longer caught. See docs/notes/release-integrity-verification.md Layer 1. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 0.

title: Install-time smoke test vs org-rule-guard.py
description: Send one known org-rule-guard.py-covered case (e.g. a .github/workflows/ write attempt) through and confirm exactly one system reports the denial, not both redundantly or neither -- confirms no conflict/confusing duplication between the two guards. Framing per user direction 2026-08-13: this is an interim step, not a permanent coexistence check -- org-rule-guard.py is expected to eventually be deprecated once this project's coverage supersedes it (see plan.md Overview, revised). Only proves the one tested case, not broader overlap elsewhere. From /plan-idea-gen run 2 (2026-08-13), docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #10.

title: Practice/dry-run mode
description: A --practice flag routing all deny verdicts through additionalContext instead of blocking, for onboarding trust-building. HARD REQUIREMENT from the kill pass: a persistent, impossible-to-miss banner printed on every guarded check while active (not just at startup), or an operator could forget to ever flip it to enforcing and believe they're protected when they aren't. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #8.

title: Codex hook adapter install
description: Wires 'icg hook' into Codex CLI's hooks.json PreToolUse config. Codex's hook API is confirmed still young/stabilizing (~5 months old) -- see docs/notes/multi-harness-integration.md. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Architecture 'Integration point'.

title: vault pack: destructive verbs
description: kv destroy, secrets disable, policy delete, token/lease revoke -- the core motivating gap. CommandRegex, both front-ends, deny-only for v1. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 1.

title: Docker destructive-ops pack
description: New rule pack (packs/docker.*) covering docker system prune -a, docker volume rm, and forced removal of tagged/in-use images -- same Pack/GuardedPattern shape as the existing Vault pack. Cleanest coverage-breadth expansion found in the whole ideation pool, zero new architecture needed. Objection: real but bounded uncertainty about how much direct Docker-CLI exposure exists in this environment versus everything already routing through Argo Workflows. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #9 (gap round G1).

title: Canary rollout via NEEDLE --identifier
description: Add a canary release channel alongside stable in the self-updater's trust pointer; launch one NEEDLE worker with --identifier canary-icg tracking it before promoting a release fleet-wide. Concrete implementation of Layer 4's deferred staged-rollout, using infrastructure that already exists for free. Objection: one canary instance may not generate enough command diversity to be meaningful alone -- it's a backstop behind CI, not the primary verification. Depends on Phase 0's trust-pointer mechanism. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #4.

title: Pack-authoring scaffold tool (icg new-pack)
description: A CLI subcommand generating a new rule-pack file with the required Pack/GuardedPattern fields pre-filled, plus a paired regression-test stub. Structurally enforces the Layer-1 'every rule needs a test' discipline instead of relying on an author remembering. Objection: may be premature at only ~9 planned packs; payoff scales with pack count. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #2.

title: Redirect dispatch: hook front-end realization
description: Maps deny/updatedInput/additionalContext onto the native PreToolUse JSON response fields (permissionDecision:deny, updatedInput, additionalContext). Both harnesses accept these fields in schema; Codex doesn't yet honor additionalContext specifically (see Phase 3). Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Components 'Redirect dispatch'.

title: Auto-denial-becomes-test
description: Every deny verdict automatically appends its command as a new regression-suite case (hook a --record-as-test path into the deny-dispatch code, writing to tests/regression/<pack-id>.cases). Requires periodic curation/pruning so the suite doesn't grow unbounded and slow CI -- do not make it permanently automatic without a pruning step. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #1.

title: tmux pack: bare NATO session targeting
description: Blocks tmux commands targeting bare NATO-alphabet session names (alpha, bravo, ...) exact-match, not suffixed worker session names. CommandRegex, both front-ends. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 1.

title: misc pack: needle cleanup detection
description: Literal command block on 'needle cleanup' (SIGHUPs live workers). CommandRegex, both front-ends. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 1.

title: Codex hook-version compatibility matrix
description: Add a matrix stage to icg-ci running the Codex hook adapter's test suite against the last 3 minor Codex CLI releases (pinned versions), failing the build on regression. Codex's PreToolUse hook is confirmed still churning (~5 months old, scope still expanding per docs/notes/multi-harness-integration.md) -- this catches breakage from Codex's own upstream changes before it silently degrades that front-end's coverage. Objection: only pays for itself while Codex's hook API keeps churning -- could become dead CI weight once it stabilizes. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #6 (gap round G4).
